title: The lungs of the planet?
description:
The lungs of the planet? The Amazon is said to make 20 per cent of the world's oxygen.

Calling it the lungs is a misconception. Forests matter a great deal, he says, but not for producing oxygen.

Net oxygen from land ecosystems is close to zero, once you count what plants and microbes use.

Half goes straight back Plants use about half of the oxygen they make. Microbes and insects breaking down plant matter use the rest.

From burial. Oxygen stays in the air when plant and algae matter is buried before it breaks down. Most burial happens in ocean sediments, where algae sink into deep sea mud.

A third of the work About a third of land photosynthesis happens in tropical forests. Researchers suggest that is how the myth began.

21 per cent oxygen. Michael Coe of the Woods Hole Research Center said the 20 per cent claim does not make any physical sense.

What it really does It stores carbon, helps steady the rain and shelters extraordinary biodiversity.

Not the lungs. The air conditioner.

Sources:
- https://nature.ox.ac.uk/research_stories/rainforests-are-not-the-lungs-of-our-planet/ (read): primary source, Yadvinder Malhi, Oxford, 3 March 2021; established that calling the Amazon the lungs of the planet is a misconception; that net oxygen production by land ecosystems is close to zero; that about half the oxygen plants make is used by the plants themselves and the other half by microbes and insects breaking down plant material; that oxygen accumulates when organic matter is buried, mostly in ocean sediments where algae sink into deep sea mud; that about a third of land photosynthesis happens in tropical forests, the Amazon being the largest; that oxygen is about 21 per cent of the air; and that forests matter for biodiversity, carbon storage, climate and water regulation but not for oxygen.
- https://www.nationalgeographic.com/environment/article/why-amazon-doesnt-produce-20-percent-worlds-oxygen (read): established that the Amazon is often said to make 20 per cent of the world's oxygen and that the article calls this a gross overestimate; Malhi's quote that the net oxygen effect of the Amazon or any other biome is around zero; Michael Coe of the Woods Hole Research Center saying the claim does not make any physical sense; and the suggestion by Malhi and Coe that the myth began with the Amazon's large share of land photosynthesis.
- https://noticiasambientales.com/environment-en/is-the-amazon-the-lungs-of-the-planet-the-scientific-myth-claiming-it-produces-20-of-the-global-oxygen/ (read): second report dated 7 November 2025; corroborated the Malhi and Coe statements, oxygen at 21 per cent of the air, and Coe's description of the forest as a giant air conditioner that stores carbon dioxide and helps steady South American rainfall.
- https://longnow.org/ideas/the-amazon-is-not-the-earths-lungs/ (read): summary of Peter Brannen in The Atlantic, 31 August 2019; corroborated that the Amazon does not supply 20 per cent of the planet's oxygen and that its net contribution is more or less zero. Not used for its 6 per cent figure.
